articles.title: It will soon be too late to regulate use of autonomous weapons, warns Red Cross
articles.description: Warning about putting ‘genie back in the bottle’ comes as UN conference fails to agree on regulation instrument The International Committee of the Red Cross and rights groups have warned that it will soon be too late to put the “genie back in the bottle” as the development of autonomous weapons appears to outpace efforts to regulate them. The stark warning came as more than 120 member states of the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons concluded a week-long conference in Geneva. Continue reading...

articles.title: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse

source.name: Frances Mao in Geneva and Patrick Wintour

articles.description: Week-long efforts fail to establish negotiating mandate on AI warfare after Russian ‘filibustering’ Week-long efforts to agree a negotiating mandate for a legally binding international treaty to control the use of autonomous weapons collapsed just before 5am after all-night talks failed to overcome Russian objections. Despite an overwhelming majority of states at the UN’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) in Geneva wanting to agree a negotiating mandate leading to a legally binding treaty, the need for consensus forced the conference to adopt a much weaker option. Continue reading...

articles.title: Pill to treat pancreatic cancer hailed as ‘biggest breakthrough in decades’
articles.description: Cancer undetectable for one in 12 patients in daraxonrasib trial, while nearly all participants’ tumours stopped growing A pill that can shrink and potentially eliminate pancreas tumours is being hailed as the biggest breakthrough treatment for the cancer in decades. In one in 12 of the patients given the drug, daraxonrasib, during a trial, the cancer became undetectable, and the tumours stopped growing in almost all of the 61 patients. The trial participants had recently been diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer that had spread to other parts of the body. Continue reading...

articles.title: Spacecraft reaches Mercury on second-ever mission to enter its orbit
articles.description: BepiColombo double probe will map planet’s surface and study its interior to shed light on its unusually large core After a voyage of more than eight years and 6bn miles, a joint European-Japanese space mission has arrived at Mercury and is preparing to swing into orbit around the tiny, barely explored world. The BepiColombo mission will become only the second in history to circle the first rock from the sun and the smallest planet in the solar system when flight controllers fire the spacecraft’s thrusters on Saturday and send it into orbit.
